posts.title: How to Safely Handle Roadside Traffic Inspections
posts.content: Roadside stops often trigger panic. The key is understanding that protocol protects both parties. Under Indian Motor Vehicle regulations and Supreme Court directives, a police officer cannot remove your ignition key or physically seize your phone without judicial warrant. Always ask politely: 'Am I being detained, Officer, or am I free to proceed?' Keep your DigiLocker verified digital documents ready.

questions.text: Can an officer seize my smartphone during a regular vehicle inspection?
questions.answer: No. Under Article 20(3) of the Constitution and the landmark Puttaswamy privacy judgment, your digital device is protected against arbitrary searches. An officer cannot force you to unlock your phone, reveal passwords, or browse through chats without a specific judicial search warrant or formal FIR seizure memo under Section 102 CrPC / Section 107 BNSS.

questions.text: What should I do if a police officer refuses to register an FIR for theft?
questions.answer: Under the Supreme Court mandate in Lalita Kumari v. Govt of UP, registration of an FIR is mandatory for cognizable offenses. If an officer refuses, you can: (1) Submit a written complaint to the Superintendent of Police (SP) under Sec 154(3) CrPC / Sec 173(3) BNSS by registered post, or (2) File an application before the Magistrate under Sec 156(3) CrPC.

questions.text: What are my exact rights during a traffic stop check, and are digital documents on DigiLocker valid?
questions.answer:
Roadside Traffic Checks & Digital Document Rights:

1. Digital Documents are 100% Legal: Producing your Driving License (DL), Registration (RC), Insurance, and PUC certificates via government DigiLocker or mParivahan apps is recognized by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH). Physical confiscation is illegal unless for major statutory suspensions.
2. Vehicle Keys: Traffic personnel are strictly prohibited from forcefully snatching keys out of your vehicle's ignition during routine verification.
3. Towing Restrictions: Towing a vehicle while any occupant is seated inside is prohibited in most metropolitan regulations; officers must issue a standard compounding challan instead.
4. E-Challan Contestation: You can contest unfair electronic traffic tickets online via the Virtual Court / Lok Adalat platform without visiting physical courtrooms.

questions.text: Do I have the constitutional right to record police officers in public spaces?
questions.answer:
Civic Shield Step-by-Step Encounter Protocol:

1. Clarify Encounter Status: Calmly ask, "Am I being detained, officer, or am I free to go?" If the officer states you are free to go, walk away peacefully.
2. Establish Reasonable Grounds: If detained, ask, "What is the specific reasonable suspicion for my detainment?" Officers must state verifiable, articulable grounds on the record.
3. Physical Search Limits: A pat-down is strictly restricted to outer clothing for officer safety unless probable cause or a valid search warrant exists. Never resist physically; state verbally: "I do not consent to any searches."
4. Mandatory Arrest Memo: Under D.K. Basu guidelines, if placed under arrest, the officer MUST prepare an Arrest Memo signed by a witness and inform one designated family member within 8-12 hours.
5. Right to Legal Counsel & Silence: You have the fundamental right to consult an advocate under Article 22(1) and the right against self-incrimination under Article 20(3).

Civic Shield Legal Guidance regarding "awesome thanks":

1. Document & Demand Written Clarity: In any administrative or official dispute, always request formal written citations instead of relying on verbal instructions.
2. Citing Authority: Ask the official, "Under what specific section of law or rule is this directive issued?" Public authorities must act strictly within statutory boundaries.
3. Procedural Remedies: You have the right to submit a formal representation, seek free legal advice through District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA/NALSA), or file an RTI petition to inspect relevant public records.
4. Support: Our team monitors questions to continuously update verified guidance templates in the Evidence Vault.
